parsed.explanation: Rate the combined national-state regime. The sharpest visitor exposure is federal entry/document screening: passports/visas require birth-sex M/F markers, and mismatch can trigger refusal, extra evidence, or permanent immigration ineligibility if treated as material misrepresentation; reports include blocked or confiscated passports and stranding. If detention or removal follows, immigration and federal corrections custody are documented as severely hostile, with care denial, abuse, and birth-sex placement. The division has no statewide bathroom ban and some executive/local protections, reducing everyday state service friction, but it does not cancel federal facilities, border, or custody rules. Courts and advocacy limit some orders but do not make the traveler regime low-risk. Minors face national payer and school pressure despite local vetoes. Overall Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal passports/visas require birth-sex M/F; X new issues ended. Officers may refuse or request evidence when documents mismatch appearance; suspected wilful misrepresentation can support permanent immigration ineligibility. Reports include passports blocked/confiscated and travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; courts and civil-liberties suits challenge; legal FAQ exists; no documented arrest for being trans at this crossing stage.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal entry screening precedes and overrides state comfort; local nondiscrimination does not preempt border adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: If detention/removal follows, federal immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse for trans men; corrections adopt conversion-style policies, care denial, birth-sex placements.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts sometimes block orders; state agencies not targeting adults; legal advocacy available.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Visa fraud or facility arrest can escalate into federal/immigration custody where national rules govern placement and care.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National rule bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Other jurisdictions criminalise bathroom trespass; first arrest handcuffed, jail in men's ward, 24h.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division has no statewide facility ban, no sex-definition exclusion, executive nondiscrimination, partial local ordinances; private settings mostly not banned.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal and state-funded facilities still follow national rules; local protections may apply but not across all jurisdictions or settings.

care_services.exposure: National funding pressure caused two hospitals to pause youth gender-affirming pharmacologic care; proposed rules may restrict public-insurance reimbursement; clinic encounters can out patients.
care_services.protection: State has no minor-care ban; governor vetoed youth-care and sports bills; state insurance/employees had coverage; mental-health services continued; multistate coalition challenges.
care_services.interaction: Adult care may remain available but minors/travel families face national payer pressure; state protections uncertain for out-of-state visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism prioritises radical pro-transgender groups; executive orders remove gender identity terms, fund threats, criminalise school supports; national public support high.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division low-risk assessment; state executive nondiscrimination; local police avoid victim gender listings; prosecutors sometimes charge gender-identity crimes via sexual orientation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat rhetoric increases border/federal scrutiny and reduces trust, while state enforcement remains comparatively non-targeting.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors may face interrupted pharmacologic care, school/health records scrutiny, and border document mismatch; guardians can be implicated by child marker/name disputes.
minors_guardians.protection: State recognizes diverse families, adoption, marriage, no minor-care ban, local protections; mental/behavioural health continues.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel amplifies document and service checks; guardian care needs and child markers can trigger federal suspicion or payer refusal.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No current documented violence against trans visitors in this division; national climate and partial local ordinances may leave street friction or under-reported harassment.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State executive and municipal nondiscrimination in places; hate-crime law covers sexual orientation; no statewide ban or policing of trans presence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If outed, police response depends on locality; federal arrest can create hostile custody even where local police are benign.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement varies by port, facility, and court status; passport and hospital cases unresolved; state/local protections patchy and visitor-specific remedies untested.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts, advocacy suits, FAQ, state multistate coalition, complaint channels; some orders enjoined; rule-of-law remains but incomplete.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Protective litigation mitigates but does not erase active federal entry, facility, and custody rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.65-A has document mismatch stopped and compensated under equality law. This case is lower: federal policy mandates birth-sex markers, mismatch can mean visa refusal/permanent fraud, courts allowed restrictions, and if detained custody is documented hostile; state protections do not neutralize federal entry.

0.55-B's secondary screening, administrative refusal, and slow appeal resemble entry friction. Here adds explicit gender-marker restriction, potential permanent ineligibility, national facility exclusion, hostile immigration/corrections custody, and counterterrorism framing; remedies are contested and visitor-specific, making it below 0.55.

0.45-A's linked biometric/deception detention exposure is comparable to universal document mismatch. This case is similar because state targeting is low and courts work, but federal custody severity and border fraud exposure keep it close to 0.45 rather than safer.

0.35-A's blanket visitor-conduct register and routine refusal is more universal than targeted visa screening. This case shares exclusion/stranding and adds possible permanent bars and abusive custody if pursued, but local protections raise it somewhat above pure 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: federal border/documents, facilities, and custody dominate; state division mitigates everyday lodging/services but cannot cancel entry screening or federally funded spaces. A mismatched marker creates routine suspicion, refusal, permanent fraud, and possible detention. Once in federal custody, documented trans-hostile conditions make severity high. Minors and families face payer-driven care pauses and school scrutiny, though local nondiscrimination and vetoes keep direct service denial uneven. The result is continuous administrative/custody exposure with partial legal recourse: Elevated Risk, below functional-remedy jurisdictions but well above criminalised/imprisonment regimes.
